301: C is correct because AWS DataSync is a managed migration service that transfers data between on-premises storage and Amazon FSx for Windows File Server using parallel, multi-threaded transfer that maximizes throughput over the shared 1 Gbps link. DataSync lets you configure a bandwidth limit so the transfer can be throttled to minimize impact on other departments, and 30 TB can realistically complete within 5 days at that link speed. Physical devices like Snowcone do not have the capacity for 30 TB in one device and do not leverage the existing network link, whereas Transfer Family provides managed file transfer protocols rather than an optimized, bandwidth-controlled migration service.
302: A is correct because Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network that caches the video clips at edge locations close to mobile users, which reduces buffering and playback issues by serving content from the nearest point of presence. CloudFront offloads retrieval work from the S3 bucket, so the app scales to many users with minimal operational overhead because the CDN is fully managed and requires no servers to run. Caching at the edge also avoids repeated transfers of large raw objects from the origin, improving overall performance for the growing user base.
303: D is correct because AWS Application Auto Scaling supports target tracking policies that automatically adjust the desired number of ECS Fargate tasks to keep a chosen metric, such as average CPU or memory utilization, at a target level. This scales out automatically to absorb the high traffic at launch and scales in as utilization decreases, which reduces costs without manual policy tuning. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling does not apply to the Fargate launch type because Fargate tasks run on AWS-managed infrastructure with no EC2 instances for the company to scale.
304: A is correct because AWS DataSync is a fully managed service that can transfer large amounts of data between NFS file systems, including between AWS Regions, with parallel transfer for speed and scheduled tasks for periodic execution. It requires no servers to provision, patch, or maintain, giving the least operational overhead for recurring Region-to-Region data movement. The alternatives involve physical one-time devices, self-managed SFTP servers, or database-specific tooling that do not fit periodic NFS transfers without added management burden.
305: C is correct because Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system that is accessed with the industry-standard SMB protocol, satisfying both the SMB access requirement and the fully managed requirement. The service handles provisioning, patching, backups, and high availability, making it the purpose-built AWS solution for shared SMB storage. Running a Windows file share on an EC2 instance is not fully managed, S3 does not natively support SMB mounts, and DataSync is a transfer service rather than a shared file system.
306: A is correct because a placement group with cluster strategy packs EC2 instances tightly together within a single Availability Zone, delivering the low latency and high network throughput needed by an in-memory database processing more than 100,000 transactions per minute. Because all instances are in the same Availability Zone, traffic between them does not incur cross-AZ data transfer charges, making this the most cost-effective network design. Spreading instances across Availability Zones with other placement strategies adds inter-AZ latency and data transfer costs that conflict with the requirements.
307: D is correct because Volume Gateway cached volumes store the primary volume data in Amazon S3 while keeping only the most recently accessed data in a local cache on the on-premises host. This means the company no longer needs to scale its on-premises iSCSI storage because the full dataset resides in AWS, while recently accessed data is still served locally with low latency. Stored volumes keep the entire dataset on premises, and the S3 File Gateway and Tape Gateway serve object-access and backup use cases rather than iSCSI block volumes with local caching.
308: B and D are correct. B is correct because the consolidated billing account functions as the management account for the organization, and Trusted Advisor in that account aggregates check results across all linked member accounts, so the finance team can review all RDS checks in one place. D is correct because the RDS Idle DB Instances check identifies On-Demand RDS instances with little or no activity, and remediating those instances directly reduces RDS costs in this scenario. The Reserved Instance optimization check applies to reserved capacity purchasing decisions rather than identifying cost waste on active On-Demand instances, and the Redshift check targets a different service.
309: A is correct because S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility into S3 storage usage and, with the advanced activity metrics available in the advanced metrics and recommendations tier, shows detailed read and write request patterns so buckets that are never or rarely accessed can be identified. It is a managed, dashboard-based analytics feature requiring no custom instrumentation, which delivers the least operational overhead. CloudWatch size metrics only show storage bytes, the console S3 dashboard lacks access-pattern detail, and CloudTrail-based analysis involves heavy log volume and setup effort.
310: B is correct because a CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as origin serves the large datasets from edge locations close to customers in North America and Europe, improving download performance. CloudFront signed URLs provide the same controlled, time-limited access model as S3 signed URLs, so access control is preserved, and cached delivery from edge locations reduces repeated S3 data transfer costs for popular objects. S3 Transfer Acceleration still incurs accelerated transfer charges on every download, so it does not reduce the associated data transfer costs.
311: C is correct because a single SNS topic with SQS queues subscribed is the classic fan-out pattern: the application publishes each quote request once, and SNS message filtering routes each message to the proper SQS queue based on quote type. SQS queues durably persist messages so quotes are not lost, and each backend application server group consumes its own queue at its own pace within the 24-hour response window. This fully managed combination separates quote types cleanly with no servers to maintain, maximizing operational efficiency while minimizing maintenance.
312: B is correct because AWS Backup is a fully managed service where a single backup plan can schedule nightly backups and automatically copy them to another Region for cross-Region recovery. Adding the EC2 instances as resources is essential because backing up an EC2 instance resource captures both the instance configuration and all attached EBS data volumes, whereas adding only the EBS volumes would omit the instance configuration required for full recovery. A managed backup plan with cross-Region copies is far more operationally efficient than writing and maintaining custom Lambda functions for snapshot orchestration.
313: C is correct because Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network built to stream content at scale to millions of users, with edge locations that provide low-latency playback on mobile devices. CloudFront signed URLs restrict content delivery to authorized users by providing time-limited, tokenized access to the streams, meeting the authorization requirement. This managed approach scales automatically with the audience and avoids the impracticality of establishing VPN tunnels for each individual mobile user.
314: B is correct because Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL automatically starts, scales compute capacity in fine-grained increments, and stops when there is no demand, so the administrator does not need to select a particular instance type. This fits the infrequent access pattern and anticipates future growth, since capacity expands as usage increases, while capacity on demand minimizes cost for idle periods. Aurora Serverless also provides minimal downtime through its managed, highly available Aurora architecture, unlike provisioned instance types that must be sized up front.
315: D is correct because Amazon Inspector is the AWS vulnerability management service that scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, and deploying the Inspector agent enables detailed host assessments. Configuring a Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports satisfies the requirement for detailed findings reports. Shield is DDoS protection, Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, and GuardDuty performs intelligent threat detection on network and API activity rather than vulnerability scanning of hosts.
316: C is correct because migrating the polling and processing script to an AWS Lambda function eliminates the continuously running EC2 instance and its idle compute costs, since Lambda only incurs charges during actual execution. Lambda automatically scales concurrency to handle a growing number of messages in the SQS queue, so processing capability is maintained as volume increases. This serverless approach reduces operational costs while preserving the ability to keep up with the queue growth.
317: A is correct because AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service where a scheduled Glue job can transform the .csv files into a format the COTS application supports and load the processed data into Amazon Redshift, which the application can query. Glue is fully managed, so there are no servers, clusters, or custom scripts to provision and maintain, giving the least operational overhead. Options based on EC2 scripts, EMR clusters, or loading data into DynamoDB either add significant management burden or store the data where the COTS application cannot query it.
318: A and D are correct. A is correct because AWS CloudTrail records the API call history across the account, capturing who provisioned oversized EC2 instances and who modified security group rules, which provides the auditable event log needed to track these user and resource changes. D is correct because AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and relationships over time, and Config rules can evaluate changes against desired compliance requirements, flagging unauthorized inventory and configuration changes as they happen. Together these services give the solutions architect both the audit trail and the configuration change tracking required.
319: A is correct because AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides interactive shell access to EC2 instances through the AWS console or CLI without any shared SSH keys, open inbound SSH ports, or bastion infrastructure. Access is governed by IAM policies and all session activity is logged, satisfying the mandate to remove shared keys while improving the audit posture. As a fully managed capability, it requires the least administrative overhead compared to maintaining bastion hosts or building custom temporary key-generation workflows.
320: A is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests data by replicating records across multiple Availability Zones and retaining them, so ingested data is not lost when an EC2 instance is rebooted. Kinesis Data Analytics (now Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink) can run continuous SQL queries over the stream, enabling the data science team to query ingested data in near real time. This combination scales to the 1 MB/s ingestion rate, avoids the durability limitations of instance store or EBS-local buffering, and does not impose the batching delay of Firehose delivery before the data becomes queryable.
